paragraphs.source_en:
152.18: Walter Savage Landor (1775-1864),John Donne (1571 or 1572-1631),
English authors.
 154.12: Gaius Valerius Catullus (84?-54? B.C.), Roman poet.
 155: apparently Tom O'Roughley is an invented character. Roughley is a prom-
ontory north of Sligo.
 155.13: Yeats departs from the usual Christian tradition, in which the archangel
Gabriel sounds the trumpet which heralds the Last Judgment and the arch-
angel Michael is the warrior angel, the conqueror of Satan.
 156.97: see Yeats's note, pp. 157.7: in Greek mythology, the Centaurs are usually depicted as having the
upper part of a human body and the four-legged body of a horse.
 158.3-4: in Irish mythology, the capital of Ulster is Emain Macha ("The Twins
of Macha"). Macha was a horse-goddess who bore twins on the site, near Armagh.
 Yeats follows the spurious story of Macha measuring the town with the pin of a
brooch, based on a folk-etymology of Emain as eo main, "precious pin."
